answer: Tie each payout seat to a licensed amateur radio callsign. Each epoch the key's low-power WSPR beacon airs a code hashed from the epoch seed, and 3+ independent WSPRnet receivers must log it with SNR and path consistent with the grid square on the license. One callsign per licensed person plus a ~$30 rig means N fake seats need N exams and N people. Failure mode: a farm keying borrowed calls from one sable-painted mast; receivers see identical paths, so co-located calls merge into one seat. Spot check: a VRF raven picks 5% of keys to re-air on a second band within 2 h.
